implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a typed hand-off point with a buffer, a sender that blocks when it is full and a receiver that blocks when it is empty, and a close that lets receivers know no more values will come. Four decisions define a channel: CAPACITY (rendezvous / bounded / conflated / unbounded), MULTIPLICITY (SPSC / MPSC / MPMC), CLOSE (who may close, what a receive after close yields), and SELECT (waiting on several operations at once, with an optional non-blocking default). The discipline: the sender owns close; every blocking operation is paired with a cancellation case; a bounded channel's capacity is the backpressure mechanism, so it must be sized to a realistic burst; and channels transfer ownership while a mutex guards genuinely shared state.
idiom_name: typed channel with (capacity, multiplicity, close, select) as its four defining contracts
code_sketch:
# The four contracts that define a channel:
#
#   capacity    rendezvous | bounded (backpressure) | conflated | unbounded
#   multiplicity SPSC | MPSC | MPMC
#   close       sender-only; receive-after-close -> zero value + ok=false; send-after-close -> error
#   select      wait on several operations at once; optional default for non-blocking

# The canonical shape:
channel = make_channel(element_type, capacity=N)

def producer():
    for item in source:
        send(channel, item)          # blocks when full -> backpressure
    close(channel)                   # the SENDER closes: receivers' range-loop ends

def consumer():
    for item in receive_all(channel): # terminates on close, not by blocking forever
        process(item)

# every blocking operation gets an escape hatch, or it is a shutdown leak:
select(receive(channel), receive(done), timeout(t))

# channels TRANSFER OWNERSHIP; a mutex guards genuinely SHARED state.
pitfalls: Never closing leaves every receiver blocked forever after the producer exits - the classic leak.
Send-after-close and double-close are errors; with multiple senders a coordinator closes after waiting for all of them.
Blocking on an empty/full channel with no counterpart (or no cancellation case) parks forever - a leak, not a backpressure.
A conflated channel silently drops values for any stream that is not 'latest value wins'.
